3. Further the petitioner in the instant supplementary affidavit submits that the petitioner had some criminal cases against him and he obtained bail in all those cases. The petitioner also granted ad-interim bail in Khilgaon Police Station Case No.47 till disposal of the Rule by a Division Bench of the High Court Division being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.16787 of 2015. However, the petitioner undertakes that he will attend the next court hearing of the cases after finishing his medical check-up in the hospital in Thailand. The proceedings of that criminal case was quashed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.12239 of 2009 although the judgment of the High Court Division was set aside by the Appellate Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.204 of 2012. Against which the petitioner preferred Criminal Review Petition No.66 of 2015 which is still pending. The petitioner has been suffering from nasal stuffiness and sleep apnoea, severe backache and external chest discomfort. The petitioner is a renowned businessman and media personality and he got offices of his NTV all over the world. The petitioner has been contributing in the economy of the country by earning and bringing lot of foreign exchange in the country but the petitioner was refused by the Immigration officer and was not permitted to leave Bangladesh. Thereby the petitioner was compelled to file writ petition and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr. Murad Reza, Additional Attorney General with S. S. Sharker, Deputy Attorney General and Mr. Arobindo Kumar Roy, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 though opposing the Rule but could not place any documents that there was any restriction or embargo upon the petitioner to leave Bangladesh. There is affidavit-in-opposition. fi led on behalf of the respondent No.2 wherein the learned Assistant Attorney General submits that the petitioner is a charge sheeted accused in Badda Police Station Case No.3(2)2015 corresponding to G.R. No.37 of 2015 and the case is pending before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and submits that the petitioner is to seek permission to go abroad before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate. He is also an accused of Khilgaon Police Station Case No.47 dated 30.01.2015 and can seek permission from that court to go abroad. The petitioner was willing to go Soudi Arabia in order to perform Holly. Hajj but from the statement made in these paragraphs it is found that the petitioner is seriously sick and needs medical treatment at Bumrungrad International Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand as such the petitioner is not so much so sick that he needs medical treatment in Thailand and the petitioner is to obtain permission from the concerned court. A medical hoard can be formed by the expert doctors of the country which can suggest whether the petitioner needs treatment outside of the country and pays that the Rule is to be discharged. 

 6. Heard the learned advocates. It appears that the petitioner wants to go abroad for treatment. There was no reason nor any explanation why he has been prevented from going abroad. Such imposition of prevention is arbitrary and without justification. His passport has neither been impounded nor are there any grounds for impounding the same. The learned advocate for the petitioner by referring a decision reported in 16 BLC (AD) 1 is identical with' the present case. Similar action was taken in refusing the petitioner into go abroad and it was challenged and it has been observed in that decision as it runs- 

 7. In this particular case, the petitioner was restricted in going abroad. There was no explanation nor any reason was given and the petitioner was going for better treatment and as such refusing to allow the petitioner to leave the country is arbitrary and without jurisdiction. Even his passport has neither been impounded nor are there any grounds for impounding the same. There is no custodial order or warrant by a court of law under the laws of the land is pending against the petitioner. There is also no specific allegation against the petitioner. Under such circumstances we do not find any reason that the petitioner will not be allowed to go abroad for better treatment while he is leaving just for treatment. The learned Deputy Attorney General along with Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondents did not state anything that there is any appreciation of any subversive activities against the petitioner. Therefore such restriction imposing upon a person from going abroad requires interference. This court being a guardian of the Constitution cannot condone such practice. In the result we find merit in this Rule.
